# Code of Conduct

## Our commitment

ZigFS welcomes contributors and users of different backgrounds and experience levels. Participation
should be respectful and free from harassment, regardless of age, disability, ethnicity, gender
identity or expression, nationality, appearance, religion, sexual orientation, or socioeconomic
background.

This code applies to project issues, pull requests, reviews, discussions, and other project-managed
spaces, as well as interactions where someone is explicitly representing the project.

## Expected behavior

- Treat others with respect and patience, including people learning the project or its tools.
- Offer specific, constructive feedback about code, ideas, and behavior.
- Disagree with proposals without attacking the people who made them.
- Accept responsibility for mistakes, consider feedback, and correct harmful behavior.
- Respect privacy, boundaries, and requests to stop unwanted contact.
- Keep discussions relevant and make room for different perspectives and communication needs.

## Unacceptable behavior

- Harassment, discriminatory remarks, slurs, threats, or encouragement of violence.
- Sexualized language or imagery, and unwanted sexual attention or advances.
- Personal attacks, sustained intimidation, trolling, or deliberate disruption of discussions.
- Publishing private information or communications without permission, including doxxing.
- Repeated unwanted contact, evasion of moderation restrictions, or retaliation against reporters.
- Using project authority to pressure, exclude, or mistreat others.

Good-faith technical disagreement, criticism of a design, and requests for evidence are welcome
when expressed respectfully.

## Reporting concerns

If you experience or witness unacceptable behavior, contact a maintainer through a private contact
method explicitly published on their GitHub profile. The repository owner's profile is
[molast](https://github.com/molast). If no private contact method is available, open an issue asking
only for a private conduct-reporting channel; do not publish incident details or personal information.

If the concern involves a maintainer, contact another uninvolved maintainer where available. For
abuse on GitHub, you may also use GitHub's reporting and blocking tools; see
[Reporting abuse or spam](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/maintaining-your-safety-on-github/reporting-abuse-or-spam).
These platform tools are also an option when no independent project contact is available.

A useful report includes links or dates, a description of what happened, relevant evidence, and
any immediate safety or privacy concerns. Share only information necessary to assess the incident.
You do not need to confront the person involved before reporting.

Security vulnerability reports should follow the separate [security policy](SECURITY.md).

## Review and enforcement

Maintainers are responsible for applying this code consistently and proportionately. A maintainer
involved in a report should not decide its outcome. Uninvolved maintainers should review available
context, ask for clarification where needed, and consider the severity, impact, and any repeated
behavior.

Depending on the circumstances, responses may include:

- A request to edit or remove inappropriate content, or a private warning.
- Removal of content, locking a discussion, or limits on participation.
- A temporary restriction or permanent ban from project-managed spaces.

Serious threats, harassment, or disclosure of private information may justify immediate action;
these responses are not a mandatory sequence. Maintainers should explain decisions to the affected
person when practical without exposing reporters or confidential evidence.

Reports should be handled discreetly, with identifying information shared only as needed to review
or address the concern. Absolute confidentiality cannot be guaranteed, including where platform
reporting or legal obligations apply. Retaliation for a good-faith report is itself a violation.

## Requests for reconsideration

A person affected by a moderation decision may request reconsideration through the same private
channel, explaining any factual errors or new context. An uninvolved maintainer should review the
request where available. Do not use public threads or repeated unwanted messages to pressure
reporters or reviewers.
